children: The ECB's decision to raise its policy rate underscores how refinancing risks and interest-cost pressures are rising for highly indebted sovereigns in the euro area and elsewhere as monetary policy tightens in the face of inflationary pressures, Scope Ratings' Eiko Sievert says in a note. "The ECB decision bolsters our view that there will be no rapid reversal of interest rates in the near term, either in Europe or the U.S.," the executive director for sovereign and public sector says. This will add to fiscal challenges for governments in many of the world's largest economies as public debt burdens have risen significantly over the past 20 years, Sievert says. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)
